parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Iron can form stable ions in the +2 and +3 oxidation states.

Explain why transition elements have variable oxidation states.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Aqueous solutions of iron(II) salts contain the complex ion $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$.

Define complex ion.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Suggest a suitable reagent for this conversion. State the type of reaction.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
$[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4(\text{OH})_2]$ is a green precipitate that turns brown on standing in air.

Table 2.1 shows electrode potentials for some electrode reactions.

Table 2.1

| electrode reaction | $E^\ominus / \text{V}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_3(\text{OH})_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4(\text{OH})_2 + \text{OH}^-$ | $-0.56$ |
| $\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 4\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons 4\text{OH}^-$ | $+0.40$ |

Use the information in Table 2.1 to explain why $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4(\text{OH})_2]$ turns brown on standing in air.
Include an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$ reacts with hydrogen peroxide as shown.

reaction 1 $2[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+} + 2\text{OH}^-$ $E^\ominus_{\text{cell}} = +1.67\text{ V}$

Calculate $\Delta G^\ominus$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, for reaction 1.
